clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse has just used a reusable blood pressure cuff for one client. The same cuff is needed for another client. What should the nurse do before using the cuff on the next client?

options.A: Clean and reprocess the cuff according to the manufacturer's instructions before using it on the next client.
options.B: Inspect the cuff for visible soil; if it appears clean, use it on the next client and reprocess it at the end of the shift.
options.C: Send the cuff for high-level disinfection before the next use because the cuff contacts the client's intact skin.
options.D: Reprocess the cuff before reuse only when the next client is on Contact Precautions; otherwise reuse it if it appears clean.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices identify reprocessing of reusable medical equipment between patients as a Standard Precaution. CDC specifically states that reusable medical equipment, including blood pressure cuffs, should be cleaned and reprocessed before use on another patient or when soiled, with reprocessing performed according to the manufacturer's instructions. Therefore, option A is the best answer. Option B incorrectly delays reprocessing when the cuff appears clean. Option C selects a disinfection level solely because the cuff contacts intact skin instead of following the device's reprocessing instructions. Option D incorrectly limits between-patient reprocessing to Contact Precautions rather than applying Standard Precautions to all patients.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply Standard Precautions by reprocessing reusable patient-care equipment according to manufacturer instructions before it is used on another client.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original item used CDC guidance explicitly written for global resource-limited settings and contained weak, cueing distractors. The revised item uses CDC Core Practices applicable in all healthcare settings and tests the directly supported requirement to reprocess reusable equipment before use on another patient.

option_audit.A: Correct. Directly matches CDC Core Practices for between-patient reprocessing and manufacturer instructions.
option_audit.B: Plausible visible-soil misconception, but CDC requires reprocessing before use on another patient even when the device does not appear soiled.
option_audit.C: Plausible overprocessing misconception, but the reprocessing method should follow the device manufacturer's instructions rather than selecting a disinfection level solely from the fact that the cuff touched intact skin.
option_audit.D: Plausible confusion with Transmission-Based Precautions, but between-patient reprocessing is part of Standard Precautions and is not restricted to clients on Contact Precautions.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer after rewrite. A is the only option that follows CDC Standard Precautions and the manufacturer-instruction requirement before reuse on another client.
cueing_check: No absolute-word cueing in the correct option; distractors are clinically adjacent misconceptions; option lengths are comparable and the correct option is not uniquely detailed by an explanatory clause.
